ch1.title: Name & Greet
ch1.desc: Create a variable to store your name, then use it to build a greeting with print().
ch1.code: name = ___ # then print a greeting print("Hello, " + ___ + "!")
guidance: Assign your name as a string: name = "Your Name"
Use + to join strings (concatenation).
Call print(...) with the greeting string.
Expected output: Hello, Alex!

ch1.title: Variables and Types
ch1.desc: Assign an integer and a float to variables, then print their types using type().
ch1.code: x = ___ # int y = ___ # float print(type(x), type(y))
guidance: Use x = 42 for an integer.
Use y = 3.14 for a float.
type(value) returns the type of a value.
Output: <class 'int'> <class 'float'>

ch1.title: Multiple Assignment
ch1.desc: Assign the same value to two variables in one line. Then assign two variables from a tuple (unpacking).
ch1.code: a = b = ___ print(a, b) x, y = ___ # tuple unpacking print(x, y)
guidance: a = b = 10 gives both a and b the value 10.
x, y = (1, 2) or x, y = 1, 2 unpacks the tuple.
Fill: e.g. 10 and (1, 2).

ch1.title: Swap Two Variables
ch1.desc: Swap the values of two variables a and b using a single line (tuple unpacking).
ch1.code: a, b = "first", "second" # swap in one line a, b = ___ print(a, b) # second first
guidance: Use a, b = b, a to swap without a temp variable.
Right side is evaluated first, then assigned to the left.

ch1.title: Arithmetic +, -, *, /, //
ch1.desc: Use +, -, *, / and // to compute: 10+5, 10-3, 4*7, 15/4 (float), 15//4 (integer division).
ch1.code: print(10 + 5, 10 - 3, 4 * 7) print(15 / 4, ___) # 3.75 and 3
guidance: / is float division; // is floor (integer) division.
Fill: 15 // 4 to get 3.

ch1.title: Modulo Operator %
ch1.desc: Use % to get the remainder. Print 17 % 5 and use it to check if a number is even (n % 2 == 0).
ch1.code: print(17 % 5) # 2 n = 8 print(n % 2 == ___) # True if even
guidance: 17 % 5 is the remainder of 17 divided by 5, i.e. 2.
Even numbers have n % 2 == 0. Fill: 0.

ch1.title: Exponent **
ch1.desc: Use ** for exponentiation. Compute 2**10 and 3**2.
ch1.code: print(2 ** 10) # 1024 print(___) # 9
guidance: 2 ** 10 is 2 to the power 10.
Fill: 3 ** 2 for 9.

ch1.title: Comparison Operators
ch1.desc: Use ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= to compare numbers. Print the results of 5 == 5 and 3 != 4.
ch1.code: print(5 == 5, 3 != 4) print(10 ___ 20, 7 ___ 7) # < and >=
guidance: == equality, != not equal.
Fill: < and >= (or use < and >= in code).

ch1.title: Logical and, or, not
ch1.desc: Use and, or, not to combine booleans. Print (True and False), (True or False), (not False).
ch1.code: print(True and False) # False print(True or False, not False)
guidance: and is True only if both are True.
or is True if at least one is True.
not flips the boolean.

ch1.title: in Operator (membership)
ch1.desc: Use 'in' to check if a value is in a list or a substring is in a string.
ch1.code: print(3 in [1, 2, 3]) print("ab" in "abc")
guidance: 3 in [1,2,3] is True.
"ab" in "abc" is True (substring).

ch1.title: is vs ==
ch1.desc: Compare is and ==. For small integers, a is b may be True; for different objects with same value, is is False.
ch1.code: a = 256 b = 256 print(a == b, a is b) x = "hi" y = "hi" print(x == y, x is y)
guidance: == compares values; is compares identity (same object).
Use == for values; use is for None: x is None.

ch1.title: += and -=
ch1.desc: Use += and -= to update a variable. Start with n=10, then n += 5 and n -= 3.
ch1.code: n = 10 n ___ 5 n ___ 3 print(n) # 12
guidance: n += 5 is the same as n = n + 5.
Fill: += and -=.

ch1.title: Chained Comparison
ch1.desc: Python allows 1 < x < 5. Write a condition that checks if n is between 10 and 20 inclusive.
ch1.code: n = 15 print(___) # True
guidance: Chained: 10 <= n <= 20 is equivalent to 10 <= n and n <= 20.
Fill: 10 <= n <= 20.

ch1.title: String Repeat with *
ch1.desc: Use * to repeat a string. Print 'ab' * 3 to get 'ababab'.
ch1.code: print("ab" * ___) # ababab
guidance: "ab" * 3 repeats the string 3 times.
Fill: 3.

ch1.title: Boolean from Comparison
ch1.desc: Comparisons return bool. Assign result of (age >= 18) to is_adult and print it.
ch1.code: age = 20 is_adult = age ___ 18 print(is_adult)
guidance: age >= 18 returns True or False.
Fill: >=.

ch1.title: Conditional Expression
ch1.desc: Use the ternary form: x if condition else y. Set label = 'even' if n%2==0 else 'odd'.
ch1.code: n = 4 label = "even" if n % 2 == 0 else "odd" print(label)
guidance: a if cond else b evaluates to a when cond is True, else b.
Result here: "even".

ch1.title: Operator Precedence
ch1.desc: Understand precedence: * before +. Compute 2 + 3 * 4 and use parentheses to get (2+3)*4.
ch1.code: print(2 + 3 * 4) # 14 print(___) # 20
guidance: 3 * 4 is done first, so 2+12=14.
Fill: (2 + 3) * 4 to get 20.

ch1.title: Membership: in with List
ch1.desc: Use 'in' to check if 3 is in [1,2,3] and if 'x' is not in 'abc'. Print both results.
ch1.code: print(3 in [1, 2, 3], "x" not in "abc")
guidance: in for membership; not in for absence.
Result: True, True.

ch1.title: String Concatenation +
ch1.desc: Use + to join two strings. Then use * to repeat a string. Print 'Hi' + '!' and 'Ha' * 2.
ch1.code: print("Hi" + "!", "Ha" * 2)
guidance: + concatenates strings.
* with int repeats the string. Result: Hi!, HaHa.

ch1.title: Lists: Append and Index
ch1.desc: Create a list, append two items, then print the first and last elements using indices.
ch1.code: items = ["a", "b"] items.append(___) items.append(___) print(items[0], items[-1])
guidance: list.append(x) adds to the end.
Index -1 is the last element.

ch1.title: Dict: Keys and Values
ch1.desc: Create a dict with name and age. Print the value for 'name' and get all keys using .keys().
ch1.code: person = {"name": "Sam", "age": 25} print(person["name"], list(person.keys()))
guidance: Access by key: person["name"].
.keys() returns a view; wrap in list() to print.

ch1.title: Tuple Creation and Unpacking
ch1.desc: Create a tuple (1, 2, 3). Unpack it into a, b, c and print a + b + c.
ch1.code: t = (1, 2, 3) a, b, c = ___ print(a + b + c)
guidance: Tuples use parentheses. Unpack: a, b, c = t.
Fill: t. Result: 6.

ch1.title: Set: Create and add
ch1.desc: Create an empty set with set(), add elements 1, 2, 2, 3 (sets have no duplicates). Print the set.
ch1.code: s = set() s.add(1) s.add(2) s.add(2) s.add(3) print(___)
guidance: set() creates an empty set (not {} which is dict).
.add(2) twice still leaves one 2. Fill: s. Result: {1, 2, 3}.

ch1.title: List Indexing and Slicing
ch1.desc: Given a list [10, 20, 30, 40], print the first element and the slice from index 1 to 3 (exclusive).
ch1.code: L = [10, 20, 30, 40] print(L[0], L[___:___]) # 10 and [20, 30]
guidance: L[0] is first. Slice L[1:3] is elements at index 1 and 2.
Fill: 1 and 3.

ch1.title: Nested List (list of lists)
ch1.desc: Create a 2x2 grid as a list of lists. Access the element in row 1, column 0.
ch1.code: grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] print(grid[___][___]) # 3
guidance: grid[1] is [3, 4]; grid[1][0] is 3.
Row index 1, column index 0.

ch1.title: Dict with Nested Dict
ch1.desc: Create a dict 'user' with key 'profile' whose value is another dict with 'name' and 'age'. Access user['profile']['name'].
ch1.code: user = {"profile": {"name": "Alex", "age": 22}} print(user["profile"]["name"])
guidance: Chain keys: user["profile"]["name"].
Nested structures are common in JSON-like data.

ch1.title: Tuple in List
ch1.desc: Create a list of tuples: [(1,'a'), (2,'b')]. Access the second tuple and then its first element.
ch1.code: pairs = [(1, "a"), (2, "b")] print(pairs[1][___]) # 2
guidance: pairs[1] is (2, 'b'). pairs[1][0] is 2.
Fill: 0.

ch1.title: Set from List (remove duplicates)
ch1.desc: Convert a list [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3] to a set to remove duplicates, then back to a sorted list.
ch1.code: L = [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3] unique = list(set(___)) unique.sort() print(unique)
guidance: set(L) removes duplicates. list(set(L)) gives a list (order may vary).
Then .sort(). Fill: L.

ch1.title: Dict .get() with Default
ch1.desc: Use .get(key, default) to safely get a value. If key is missing, return 0.
ch1.code: d = {"a": 1, "b": 2} print(d.get("a", 0), d.get("c", ___))
guidance: d.get("c", 0) returns 0 when "c" is not in d.
Fill: 0.

ch1.title: List Slice [start:end:step]
ch1.desc: Given [0,1,2,3,4,5], use slicing to get [2,3,4] and then every second element [0,2,4].
ch1.code: L = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] print(L[2:5], L[___:___:___])
guidance: L[2:5] is [2,3,4]. L[0:6:2] or L[::2] is [0,2,4].
Fill: 0, 6 (or leave blank), 2.

ch1.title: Empty list, dict, tuple, set
ch1.desc: Create empty list [], empty dict {}, empty tuple (), and empty set set(). Print their types.
ch1.code: print(type([]), type({}), type(())) print(type(set()))
guidance: {} is an empty dict; empty set must be set().
() is the empty tuple.

ch1.title: List of Tuples to Dict
ch1.desc: Convert a list of pairs [(1,'a'), (2,'b')] into a dict {1:'a', 2:'b'} using dict().
ch1.code: pairs = [(1, "a"), (2, "b")] d = dict(___) print(d)
guidance: dict(pairs) builds a dict from key-value pairs.
Fill: pairs.

ch1.title: Mutable vs Immutable (tuple)
ch1.desc: Tuples are immutable. Lists are mutable. Change L[0] in a list; tuples cannot be changed.
ch1.code: t = (1, 2) L = [1, 2] L[0] = 9 print(t[0], L[0])
guidance: Tuple elements cannot be reassigned; list elements can.
Result: 1, 9.

ch1.title: Inner List and Tuple Access
ch1.desc: Given data = ([1, 2], (3, 4)), change the list's first element and print the tuple's second element.
ch1.code: data = ([1, 2], (3, 4)) data[0][0] = 99 print(data[0], data[1][1])
guidance: data[0] is the list (mutable). data[1][1] is 4.

ch1.title: Set from String
ch1.desc: Use set('hello') to get unique characters. Print the set and its length.
ch1.code: chars = set("hello") print(chars, len(chars))
guidance: set("hello") gives unique letters. len is 4.

ch1.title: range() Basics
ch1.desc: Use range(5) to get numbers 0 through 4. Convert to list and print it.
ch1.code: r = range(5) print(list(r)) # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
guidance: range(5) produces 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (stop is exclusive).
Wrap in list() to see the values.

ch1.title: range() with start and stop
ch1.desc: Use range(2, 7) to get numbers from 2 up to (but not including) 7. Convert to list and print.
ch1.code: r = range(2, 7) print(list(r)) # [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
guidance: range(start, stop): start is inclusive, stop is exclusive.
range(2, 7) gives 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

ch1.title: range() with start, end, step
ch1.desc: Use range(0, 10, 2) to get even numbers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. The third argument is the step. Convert to list and print.
ch1.code: r = range(0, 10, 2) print(list(r)) # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]
guidance: range(start, end, step): step is the increment (default 1).

ch1.title: len() and str()
ch1.desc: Use len() to get the length of a string and a list. Use str() to convert a number to a string.
ch1.code: word = "hello" print(len(word), len([1,2,3])) print(str(42) + " eggs")
guidance: len(sequence) returns the number of elements.
str(42) converts to "42".

ch1.title: int() and float()
ch1.desc: Convert the string '42' to int and '3.14' to float. Print their sum.
ch1.code: print(int("42") + float("3.14"))
guidance: int("42") is 42; float("3.14") is 3.14.

ch1.title: bool()
ch1.desc: Use bool() to convert values to True/False. Which of 0, 1, '', 'hi', [], [1] are truthy?
ch1.code: print(bool(0), bool(1), bool(""), bool("hi")) print(bool([]), bool([1]))
guidance: Falsy: 0, "", [], None, False. Everything else is truthy.
bool([1]) is True (non-empty list).

ch1.title: list() from range
ch1.desc: Use list(range(5)) to create [0,1,2,3,4]. Then list(range(2, 6)) for [2,3,4,5].
ch1.code: print(list(range(5))) print(list(range(2, ___)))
guidance: range(5) is 0..4; range(2, 6) is 2,3,4,5.
Fill: 6.

ch1.title: tuple() and set()
ch1.desc: Convert [1, 2, 3] to a tuple using tuple() and to a set using set().
ch1.code: L = [1, 2, 3] print(tuple(L), set(L))
guidance: tuple(L) returns (1, 2, 3).
set(L) returns {1, 2, 3}.

ch1.title: str.join()
ch1.desc: Use ','.join(['a','b','c']) to get 'a,b,c'. Use ' '.join for space-separated words.
ch1.code: words = ["Hello", "world"] print(" ".join(___))
guidance: separator.join(iterable) joins strings.
Fill: words. Result: "Hello world".

ch1.title: sorted()
ch1.desc: Use sorted() on a list of numbers and on a list of strings. sorted() returns a new list.
ch1.code: print(sorted([3, 1, 2])) print(sorted(["banana", "apple"]))
guidance: sorted([3,1,2]) returns [1, 2, 3].
Strings are sorted lexicographically.

ch1.title: min(), max(), sum()
ch1.desc: Use min, max, and sum on a list of numbers [10, 20, 30].
ch1.code: nums = [10, 20, 30] print(min(nums), max(nums), sum(nums))
guidance: min and max work on any comparable iterable.
sum adds numbers. Result: 10, 30, 60.

ch1.title: abs() and round()
ch1.desc: Use abs(-5) and round(3.7). Try round(3.14159, 2) for two decimal places.
ch1.code: print(abs(-5), round(3.7)) print(round(3.14159, ___))
guidance: abs(-5) is 5.
round(3.14159, 2) is 3.14. Fill: 2.

ch1.title: input() and int()
ch1.desc: Use input() to read a string (e.g. user's name). Use input() and int() to read a number.
ch1.code: name = input("Name? ") # num = int(input("Number? ")) print(name)
guidance: input(prompt) returns a string. Use int(input(...)) for integers.
In real code: num = int(input("Number? ")).

ch1.title: type()
ch1.desc: Use type(x) to get the type of a value. Print type(5), type('hi'), type([1,2]).
ch1.code: print(type(5), type("hi"), type([1, 2]))
guidance: type(5) is <class 'int'>.
Use isinstance(x, int) to check type.

ch1.title: range() and for
ch1.desc: Use range(5) in a for loop to print numbers 0 through 4.
ch1.code: for i in range(5): print(___)
guidance: range(5) produces 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
Fill: i.

ch1.title: enumerate()
ch1.desc: Use enumerate(['a','b','c']) to get (index, item) pairs. Print index and item in a loop.
ch1.code: for i, x in enumerate(["a", "b", "c"]): print(i, x)
guidance: enumerate(seq) yields (0, a), (1, b), (2, c).
Use when you need both index and value.

ch1.title: zip()
ch1.desc: Use zip([1,2], ['a','b']) to pair elements. Loop and print each pair.
ch1.code: for n, c in zip([1, 2], ["a", "b"]): print(n, c)
guidance: zip(a, b) yields (a[0], b[0]), (a[1], b[1]), ...
Stops at the shortest sequence.

ch1.title: dict() from keys
ch1.desc: Use dict.fromkeys(['a','b'], 0) to create {'a':0, 'b':0}.
ch1.code: d = dict.fromkeys(["a", "b"], ___) print(d)
guidance: dict.fromkeys(keys, value) gives each key the same value.
Fill: 0.

ch1.title: reversed() and list()
ch1.desc: Use list(reversed([1,2,3])) to get [3, 2, 1].
ch1.code: print(list(reversed([1, 2, 3])))
guidance: reversed(seq) returns a reverse iterator.
Wrap in list() to see the result.

ch1.title: divmod()
ch1.desc: Use divmod(17, 5) to get both quotient and remainder in one call. It returns (3, 2).
ch1.code: q, r = divmod(17, 5) print(q, r) # 3 2
guidance: Useful for splitting into quotient and remainder.

ch1.title: pow() or **
ch1.desc: Use pow(2, 10) for 2**10. Optionally pow(2, 10, 1000) for (2**10) % 1000.
ch1.code: print(pow(2, 10)) print(pow(2, 10, ___)) # 24
guidance: pow(2, 10) is 1024.

ch1.title: range: start, stop, step
ch1.desc: Use range(2, 11, 2) to get even numbers 2 to 10. Convert to list and print. Then use negative step: range(5, 0, -1).
ch1.code: print(list(range(2, 11, 2))) # [2,4,6,8,10] print(list(range(5, 0, ___))) # [5,4,3,2,1]
guidance: range(start, stop, step): stop is exclusive.
Negative step counts down. Fill: -1.

ch1.title: Tuple: immutability and indexing
ch1.desc: Create t = (10, 20, 30). Print t[1] and t[-1]. Try t[1] = 99 (will raise TypeError — tuples are immutable).
ch1.code: t = (10, 20, 30) print(t[1], t[-1]) # 20 30 # t[1] = 99 TypeError
guidance: Tuples are immutable: you cannot assign to t[i].
Indexing and slicing work; t[1] is 20, t[-1] is 30.

ch1.title: List: mutability and in-place methods
ch1.desc: Create L = [1, 2, 3]. Use L.append(4), L.insert(0, 0), then L.pop(). Print L.
ch1.code: L = [1, 2, 3] L.append(4) L.insert(0, 0) L.pop() print(L) # [0, 1, 2, 3]
guidance: Lists are mutable. append(4) adds at end; insert(0, 0) at start; pop() removes and returns last.

ch1.title: bool: truthiness and bool()
ch1.desc: Use bool() on 0, 1, '', 'hi', [], [1]. Print bool(0), bool(''), bool([1]). Know: empty sequences are False.
ch1.code: print(bool(0), bool(""), bool([1])) # False False True
guidance: bool(0) and bool('') are False; bool([1]) is True.
Empty list [], empty string '', 0, None are falsy.

ch1.title: String: immutability and slicing
ch1.desc: s = 'python'. Print s[0], s[-1], s[1:4]. Strings are immutable — s[0] = 'P' would raise TypeError.
ch1.code: s = "python" print(s[0], s[-1], s[1:4]) # p n yth # s[0] = "P" TypeError
guidance: Strings are immutable. Read with s[i] or s[a:b]; to change, build a new string.
s[1:4] is 'yth' (indices 1,2,3).

ch1.title: Dictionary: keys, values, items
ch1.desc: d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}. Print list(d.keys()), list(d.values()), list(d.items()). Add d['c'] = 3 and get d.get('c', 0).
ch1.code: d = {"a": 1, "b": 2} print(list(d.keys()), list(d.values())) d["c"] = 3 print(d.get("c", 0)) # 3
guidance: .keys(), .values(), .items() return views; wrap in list() to print.
d.get('c', 0) returns value or default; d['c']=3 then get gives 3.

ch1.title: Dictionary: update and copy
ch1.desc: d = {1: 'a'}. Use d.update({2: 'b', 3: 'c'}). Create a shallow copy with d2 = d.copy() or dict(d). Print d, d2.
ch1.code: d = {1: "a"} d.update({2: "b", 3: "c"}) d2 = d.copy() print(d, d2) # {1:a, 2:b, 3:c}
guidance: d.update(other) merges key-value pairs into d.
d.copy() or dict(d) makes a shallow copy.

ch2.title: if / else
ch2.desc: Write an if/else that prints 'Adult' if age >= 18, else 'Minor'.
ch2.code: age = ___ if age >= 18: print("Adult") else: print("Minor")
guidance: Use if condition: and else: with a colon.
Indent the body (4 spaces).
Set age = 20 or age = 10 to test both branches.

ch2.title: elif Chain
ch2.desc: Use if / elif / else to print 'small', 'medium', or 'large' based on a number n.
ch2.code: n = ___ if n < 10: print("small") elif n < 100: print("medium") else: print("large")
guidance: elif is short for else-if; only one branch runs.
Test with n=5 (small), n=50 (medium), n=200 (large).

ch2.title: Nested if
ch2.desc: Use a nested if: if x > 0, then check if x is even; print 'positive even' or 'positive odd'. Else print 'non-positive'.
ch2.code: x = ___ if x > 0: if x % 2 == 0: print("positive even") else: print("positive odd") else: print("non-positive")
guidance: Put an if inside another if block (nested).
Test with x=4 (positive even), x=3 (positive odd), x=-1 (non-positive).

ch2.title: Multiple Conditions with and
ch2.desc: Print 'in range' if n is between 1 and 10 (inclusive), else 'out of range'.
ch2.code: n = ___ if n >= 1 and n <= 10: print("in range") else: print("out of range")
guidance: Combine conditions with and.
Alternatively use 1 <= n <= 10 (chained comparison).

ch2.title: Multiple Conditions with or
ch2.desc: Print 'weekend' if day is 'Saturday' or 'Sunday', else 'weekday'.
ch2.code: day = ___ if day == "Saturday" or day == "Sunday": print("weekend") else: print("weekday")
guidance: or is True if at least one condition is True.
Test with day="Saturday" or "Monday".

ch2.title: Ternary (if-else expression)
ch2.desc: Use a one-line conditional: assign status = 'pass' if score >= 60 else 'fail'. Print status.
ch2.code: score = ___ status = "pass" if score >= 60 else "fail" print(status)
guidance: a if cond else b is the ternary form.
Test with score=70 (pass) and score=50 (fail).

ch2.title: Empty vs Non-empty
ch2.desc: If a list L is non-empty, print its first element; else print 'empty list'.
ch2.code: L = ___ # e.g. [1,2,3] or [] if L: print(L[0]) else: print("empty list")
guidance: Empty list [] is falsy; non-empty list is truthy.
So if L: is a common Python idiom.

ch2.title: if with not
ch2.desc: Print 'invalid' if age is not between 0 and 120. Otherwise print 'valid'.
ch2.code: age = ___ if not (0 <= age <= 120): print("invalid") else: print("valid")
guidance: not (condition) inverts the boolean.
You can also write if age < 0 or age > 120.

ch2.title: for over a List
ch2.desc: Loop over a list of names and print each name with a greeting.
ch2.code: names = ["Ali", "Bo", "Cat"] for name in names: print("Hi, " + ___)
guidance: for item in sequence: iterates over each element.
Use the loop variable name in the print. Fill: name.

ch2.title: for with range(n)
ch2.desc: Use for i in range(5) to print 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
ch2.code: for i in range(5): print(___)
guidance: range(5) yields 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
Fill: i.

ch2.title: for with range(start, end)
ch2.desc: Loop from 2 to 6 (exclusive) using range(2, 6) and print each number.
ch2.code: for n in range(2, 6): print(___)
guidance: range(2, 6) gives 2, 3, 4, 5.
Fill: n.

ch2.title: for with range step
ch2.desc: Use range(0, 10, 2) to print even numbers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
ch2.code: for x in range(0, 10, 2): print(___)
guidance: range(start, stop, step) — step of 2 skips every other.
Fill: x.

ch2.title: Sum with for
ch2.desc: Loop over nums = [10, 20, 30] and compute the sum. Print the sum.
ch2.code: nums = [10, 20, 30] total = 0 for n in nums: total = total + ___ print(total) # 60
guidance: Initialize total = 0, then add each n in the loop.
